newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent slumps on German sale news then recovers.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent slumps on German sale news then recovers.

text.p: IPE Brent futures recovered some of Thursday's losses on short-covering during the afternoon session after slumping earlier on news that Germany planned to sell some of its strategic oil reserves.

August Brent was trading at $17.98 a barrel, or 24 cents a barrel down, having hit a session low of $17.85 earlier in the day after German government sources said that Bonn expected raise some 400 million marks ($230 million) from the sale of some oil reserves this year.
"The market moved lower on the German news and now is awaiting for confirmation on the terms, conditions and timing," a trader said, adding that he expected a further move to the downside.
Traders said August Brent was helped later in the day by some buying to cover short positions.
"We had some fund selling earlier but people started to buy again so there was a techincal bounce on some short covering," a trader said.
NYMEX WTI, which was called to open lower on a weaker IPE, fell to $19.05 but moved back up to $19.26, or 20 cents down.
Oil industry sources said that the German plan to sell oil from its stocks in 1997 amd 1998 would release at least 75,000 barrels per day on to the market for the remainder of the year.

Analysts said the sale would depress oil markets which are already feeling the strain of rising industry stocks, slackening U.S. demand for gasoline and the prospect of a resumption of Iraqi exports under a U.N. oil-for-food plan.
A number of traders however played down the effect of the German news, with some saying that it was an add-on in the absence of any clear fundameantal items today.
"Actually by the time the story was absorbed by the market, crude futures started to creep back up," a trader said.
"Sure it is a significant amount but the United States also is eating up a lot of oil," he said, adding he expected Brent to hold above key support at $17.85 and WTI to move back up to around $19.50.
